introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators or Phones are NOT allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the difference between

(i) Intranet and extranet. (2 marks)

(ii) The internet and World Wide Web (WWW) (2 marks)

(iii) Browser and Search engine. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Intranet and extranet (2 marks).**

- An **intranet** is a private network inside one organisation (for example a school or a company), built with Internet technology and open only to its own staff or members, who share files, notices and applications.
- An **extranet** is an extension of the intranet that lets selected outside users (suppliers, customers, partners) reach part of the organisation's network over the Internet, with a username and password.

Difference: an intranet is for internal users only, an extranet also gives controlled access to authorised external users.

**(ii) The Internet and the World Wide Web (2 marks).**

- The **Internet** is the worldwide network of interconnected networks (cables, routers, servers) that carries many services: email, file transfer, messaging, the Web.
- The **World Wide Web** is only one of those services: a collection of web pages and other documents, linked by hyperlinks, stored on web servers and viewed with a browser using the HTTP protocol.

Difference: the Internet is the infrastructure, the Web is a service that runs on it.

**(iii) Browser and search engine (2 marks).**

- A **browser** is a program (for example Chrome or Firefox) used to open, retrieve and display web pages when a user types a web address (URL).
- A **search engine** is a website or program (for example Google or Bing) that searches an index of web pages for keywords typed by the user and returns a list of matching links.

Difference: the browser displays web pages; the search engine finds pages (and is itself used through the browser).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Give two advantages and two disadvantages of using social media in a school. (4 marks)

(ii) State any two social media platforms. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Social media in a school (4 marks: 1 mark for each point).**

Advantages (any two):

- Students and teachers can communicate and share notes, assignments and announcements quickly, even outside school hours.
- Students can work together in groups and learn from videos, discussions and educational pages.
- The school can promote its activities and reach parents easily.

Disadvantages (any two):

- Students may be distracted from their studies and waste time.
- There is a risk of cyberbullying and of seeing inappropriate content.
- Private information may be exposed and false information can spread quickly.

**(ii) Two social media platforms (2 marks).** Any two of: Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, Twitter (X), YouTube, LinkedIn, TikTok.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is Computer Generation? (2 marks)

(ii) State the main technology that characterizes the 2nd and 3rd computer generations. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Computer generation (2 marks).** A computer generation is a stage in the development of computers, identified by the main electronic technology used to build the hardware. Each new generation brought computers that were smaller, faster, cheaper and more reliable.

**(ii) Main technologies (2 marks).**

- **2nd generation** (about 1956-1963): **transistors** replaced vacuum tubes.
- **3rd generation** (about 1964-1971): **integrated circuits (ICs)**, many transistors on one silicon chip.

(For reference: the 1st generation used vacuum tubes and the 4th used microprocessors.)
